title: Just Dashboard
excerpt: A self-hosted dashboard for one Linux server. Metrics, Docker, deployments, databases, a real shell, files and git, behind one login on your private network.
content_html:
Run your whole server from one tab.

Deploy apps, run Docker, manage databases and open a real shell. Self-hosted, open source, and only reachable on your private network.

Install in two minutesView on GitHub

The real interface, recorded on an example server.

paid features in Just Dashboard. Every one is free

The pages you will actually live in.

Six of them, recorded from the real interface. Pick one, or let them play through.

Push to deploy, with a preview per pull request.

Point it at a repository, an image, a Compose file or one of 157 templates. Every release is immutable, so rollback reactivates what ran before, and web services get a health-gated cutover.

It answers the next question.

Most panels show you a number and leave the reading to you. Sixty-eight percent CPU, exit code 137, restarted twelve times.

Just Dashboard says the server is waiting rather than merely busy, that a container was killed for its memory limit and what the limit was. Where it can fix a finding, the finding comes with a button.

And the rest of the machine.

Processes, logs, schedules, the firewall, backups and the dashboard's own updates, each drawn as what it is. Press a picture to see the whole page.

157 reviewed templates, each one saying how you get in.

One click each. Every card says whether you create the first account yourself, sign in with a password or token this server generated, or find no sign-in page at all.

Read the catalogue on GitHub

  • Uptime Kuma

    Self-hosted uptime monitoring.

    You create the first account

  • Grafana

    Dashboards for your metrics and logs.

    Password generated here

  • Vaultwarden

    A password manager that needs its own public URL.

    Token generated here

And 121 more, from password managers to game servers.

Root-equivalent, and built like it.

Anyone who reaches it with a valid session has root on the machine. So it sits behind your VPN or an SSH tunnel, and that is enforced rather than recommended.

JD_ALLOWED_CIDRS=100.64.0.0/10,127.0.0.1/32,::1/128

Six checks stand between a request and a root shell.

In the order a request meets them, from the network it arrives on to the record it leaves behind.

  1. Tailscale by default

    Invisible to the internet, answering on your tailnet with a real certificate.

  2. Allowlist before authentication

    The API refuses every address outside the allowlist, before the login form is served.

  3. Two-factor, enforced

    An enrolled account is always asked for its code. A policy decides who must enrol.

  4. Three roles, checked on the route

    Read-only, limited and admin, enforced on the API and never in the interface alone.

  5. Typed confirmations

    Destructive actions pause. The unrecoverable ones want a typed phrase, checked server-side.

  6. An audit log for every change

    Every state-changing request is recorded with who, what and when. Sign-ins too.

Just Hub

Every server you run, on one private page.

Just Hub runs on one of your servers and brings every Just Dashboard together: their health side by side, alerts that notice a server gone quiet, and updates rolled out across all of them. It lives on your tailnet, and every server keeps its own dashboard and sign-in.

  • The fleet at a glance

    Every server's latest report side by side, with the ones that need you sorted to the top.

  • Alerts from the outside

    It notices a server that stopped reporting, which that server cannot tell you itself.

  • Updates across the fleet

    Roll a release out to one server or all of them, restart containers, run backups.

  • Servers call in, never out

    Once connected, a server reports to the hub over your tailnet, and the hub never opens a connection back.

Free for 2 servers, with every feature. Your first hub starts a 14-day Max trial, no card. Just Dashboard itself stays free and open source.

Two commands, then a login on your tailnet.

The installer guides you through private access, the first account and optional settings, and prints how to get in.

Needs a Linux server with sudo. Follow the 0.9.0 install guide to set up patch update checks. To upgrade later: git pull && docker compose up -d --build

  1. Tailscale is the default.

    The machine stays invisible to the internet and the dashboard answers on your tailnet with a real certificate. No port is opened.

  2. An SSH tunnel is the fallback.

    Served on loopback. The installer generates the master key and a first password, builds the stack, and prints the command to get in.

  3. Upgrading keeps everything.

    Your configuration, database, accounts and sessions survive the in-app update, a pull and rebuild, or running the installer again.

Free, and every feature stays free.

Just Dashboard is AGPL-3.0 and built by one person. The code, the changelog and the issue tracker are all in one place.
